Internal helper: each table's page and fit in a document

Source: R/tables.R
dot-jst_docx_layout.Rd

Each table gets the page it needs (Session 406): the setting is its own style's landscape (the style it was built under, a call's own setting included), read for its table type, so a table built with landscape = "yes" keeps its page in any document; under auto it turns only when the table cannot fit the portrait text width at the style's size with half its padding and its labels on two lines (ruling R55). landscape given – the setting in the call that writes the document – sets every page. Until Session 406 a document had one orientation, so one wide table turned every page. A table wider than its page is fitted to it (.jst_docx_fit()). The paper is the document style's. A table narrower than its caption row's title widens to it, every column in proportion, as far as its page allows (Session 407), so the title keeps one line.

Usage

.jst_docx_layout(tables, style, landscape = NULL)

Arguments

tables

A list of jst_table, and of jst_figure (a figure's page and size, .jst_figure_layout()).

style

The document's style.

landscape

NULL, or "auto", "yes" or "no" for every page.

Value

A list, one element per table: style (the table's), landscape (logical), page, fit (widths, size and note_size; size NULL when the table fits as it is), natural (the widths before any fit) and size0 (the style's size).
